correctness.rationale: The strictly positive K eigenvalues and damping make A Hurwitz, giving unique centered stationary Gaussian covariance. The bundled verifier evaluates all sixteen Lyapunov residuals, Wick variance, rational SNR, derivative factorization and maximizing substitution with 219 exact algebraic/rational checks. The denominator coefficients are positive; the sole positive derivative root has positive-to-negative sign and zero endpoint limits. The temperature-contrast inequalities prove a strict optimum offset and sharp limit. Numerical checks alone are not used as proof.

originality.rationale: Across accessible full primary texts and public research records, the exact all-parameter stationary one-time SNR peak and its strict shift from the established mean-current peak were not covered. The 2021 paper’s fluctuation is time-integrated, not instantaneous. The 2026 ellipsoid study is the closest conceptual source but full-text inspection failed; its possibly covering spherical specialization is recorded as a substantial unresolved priority risk, not suppressed.
residual_risks: arXiv:2606.17554 original full text could not be inspected; a broader ellipsoid SNR analysis may reduce to an equivalent spherical case. An exact published specialization would defeat originality.
A closed analytic stationary covariance is known prior work, so the finding is an additional optimization classification rather than a new stochastic model or independent Gaussian theory.
Source-access restrictions and record-index limits prevent an unconditional first-publication claim.

value.rationale: Experimental gyrator transport is optimized at a mean-current damping, but standardized rotation in an instantaneous frame is a distinct measurable performance objective. The theorem classifies the entire stable nonequilibrium parameter range, gives a universal explicit optimal rate and strict separation with sharp contrast bound; this is a motivated observational/control distinction rather than an arbitrary computed parameter slice. It does not claim time-average performance or a general heat-engine TUR.
